rule: स् becomes ष् after any vowel except अ/आ, or after क् or र्
explanation: Three things must hold: (1) the sound just before the स् is a vowel other than अ/आ, or क-varga, र् or ल्; (2) the स् is neither word-final nor followed by र् (so तिस्रः and तमिस्र keep their स्); (3) only anusvāra, visarga or a sibilant may intervene. Note the contrast with ṇatva, which reaches across vowels, क-varga, प-varga, य् व् and ह् — here the trigger must otherwise be immediately adjacent. हिंस् and पुंस् are lexical exceptions.
analysis: trigger इ (a vowel other than अ/आ) · nothing intervening

rule: Blocked: त् is not one of the sounds that trigger ṣatva
explanation: The ending -सु retroflexes only when the sound just before it is a trigger. Compare अग्नि + सु → अग्निषु (the vowel इ triggers) and वाक् + सु → वाक्षु (क् triggers); after त् nothing happens, so मरुत्सु keeps its dental स्.
analysis: trigger would have to be त् — not in the set · स् stays dental

rule: न् becomes ण् after र् ऋ ॠ or ष् in the same word
explanation: Three things must all hold: (1) a trigger — र् ऋ ॠ or ष् — earlier in the same word; (2) the न् is followed by a vowel or by न् म् य् व्; (3) only vowels, क-varga, प-varga, य् व् ह् or anusvāra stand in between. Any other intervening sound — a palatal, cerebral, dental, ल् श् or स् — blocks it.
analysis: trigger र् · through अ ह् म् (ह् + प-varga) · न् before आ

explanation: Compare चर् + अन → चरण. The trigger र् and the intervening अ are the same in both; here the न् is followed by त्, which is not one of the permitted following sounds, so it stays dental. This is also why a word-final न् never retroflexes — nothing follows it.

rule: Blocked: an intervening palatal, cerebral or dental stops ṇatva
explanation: The र् of अर्- would retroflex the न् of the ending, but the palatal ज् stands between them and is not one of the permitted intervening sounds — hence अर्जुनेन, never अर्जुणेन. Compare राम + एन → रामेण, where only the labial म् intervenes and does not block.
analysis: trigger र् · through ज् (palatal) — condition 3 FAILS
